verdict.line: You lose if you facetank extended trades and let Darkness Rise proc off three landed hits before backing off; you win if you land E's stun-into-Q reset while his W shield is empty and burst him down fast.

brief.thesis: Mordekaiser's W (Indestructible) constantly banks the damage he deals and takes into a shield he can consume to heal, so any trade that doesn't nearly kill him in one window just refuels his sustain. Irelia's answer is to stack Ionian Fervor and chain E's stun-and-Mark into a Q reset for one short, decisive burst rather than grinding an extended fight, then dash out with Q before his passive, Darkness Rise, procs off three landed hits and turns on his damage aura and move speed. That structural coin-flip is why the head-to-head sits almost exactly at 49.9% over 712 games even though Irelia carries the lane-advantage tag — the tools to win are real, but the margin is thin.

theirWindow.when: After his second landed hit on you
theirWindow.what: Back off immediately with Q's dash-heal before the third hit procs his passive, since the damage aura and move speed it grants flip an extended trade in his favor.

yourWindow.when: When his W hasn't refreshed recently
yourWindow.what: Engage with E's stun-and-Mark into an immediate Q reset; without a freshly banked shield to consume for healing, your burst window actually kills instead of just chipping his health bar.

start.why: The highest win rate start (49.4% over 780 games, 86.1% pick) — the extra sustain matters because you're trading in short bursts and healing off Q, not soaking prolonged exchanges with a tankier laner.

boots.why: Preferred at 49% over 584 games and 71.3% pick — Mordekaiser is a magic damage laner, and the flat magic resist directly blunts Obliterate poke and his passive damage aura.

core.why: Leads the top-performing build path (57.4% over 129 games) — current-health damage and the active slow both matter for landing a kill window before he can pop his W shield to heal back.
Rewards split-pushing and wave pressure, which forces him to either give up lane priority or come punish you into your wall zoning.
Stacks magic resist against his all-magic kit while adding attack speed that feeds Ionian Fervor stacking for the bonus on-hit damage.

he's snowballing and threatening a kill with Realm of Death

runes.keystoneWhy: Ramping adaptive damage and healing over a fight rewards Irelia's dive-and-stay pattern against a duelist with his own shield-based sustain — you need the extra damage and lifesteal to actually outlast his W.

summoners.why: The dominant pick (85.3% pick rate, 48.3% win rate) — Ignite punishes his W heal by cutting it and helps close out the even solo-kill matchup. Exhaust+Flash (9.6% pick, 45.9% win rate) is the alternative if you'd rather blunt his Realm of Death burst than secure kills.

playing.title: Hold E for stun-into-Q
playing.detail: Flawless Duet's converging blades stun and Mark, and a Marked target refreshes Bladesurge's cooldown on hit. Save E as your engage tool and follow every landed E immediately with Q for the full burst window instead of poking with it randomly.

playing.title: Break trades before his third hit
playing.detail: Darkness Rise triggers after he lands three attacks or spells on you, granting a damage aura and move speed. Count his hits during any trade and disengage with Q's dash-heal before that third one lands.

playing.title: Engage only when his shield is thin
playing.detail: Indestructible banks damage dealt and taken into a consumable heal, so a full trade into a freshly-refreshed shield just feeds him sustain. Wait for a window where he hasn't recently dealt or taken damage before committing.

playing.title: Respect Death's Grasp range
playing.detail: E pulls all enemies caught in its area at 700 range. Don't hover at that distance when it's up, or he'll yank you in for free stacks toward his passive.

playing.title: Play around his ult timer after 6
playing.detail: Realm of Death drags you into an isolated fight and steals a portion of your stats on a long cooldown (140/120/100/90/80s). Don't overextend while it's up, and once it's on cooldown you get a multi-minute window to punish freely.

playing.title: Use R's wall to zone, not just burst
playing.detail: After Vanguard's Edge hits, the resulting wall damages and slows anyone who walks through it. Drop it to cut off his engage path or seal a kill during a dive rather than only using it for the initial damage.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, rune, summoner, and win-rate numbers are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG; the mechanical reasoning and trade timing are this brief's own tactical read, not sourced data.
